Definition: to cheat; by analogy, to maltreat
BiblicalUsage: Jacob fears his father will think he is mocking him, a deceiver playing the blind man for a fool. Centuries later the chronicler says Israel mocked the messengers of God and despised His words, until there was no remedy. The word is mockery that cheats: treating what is holy as a joke, and other people as fools.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mockery is the sin this word names most sharply: it does not only disobey God, it laughs at Him, and the chronicler shows where that road ends.
